\section*{Question 1}
\begin{itemize}
\item[] Let \(f\) and \(g\) be the functions given by \(f(x)=1+\sin (2 x)\) and \(g(x)=e^{x / 2}\). Let \(R\) be the shaded region in the first quadrant enclosed by the graphs of \(f\) and \(g\) as shown in the figure above.
\item[(a)] Find the area of \(R\).
\item[(b)] Find the volume of the solid generated when \(R\) is revolved about the \(x\)-axis.
(c) The region \(R\) is the base of a solid. For this solid, the cross sections perpendicular to the \(x\)-axis are semicircles with diameters extending from \(y=f(x)\) to \(y=g(x)\). Find the volume of this solid.
![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/68363adc-2532-430c-97d8-218cc42a6dc7-1.jpg?height=550&width=443&top_left_y=361&top_left_x=1444)
\item[] The graphs of \(f\) and \(g\) intersect in the first quadrant at \((S, T)=(1.13569,1.76446)\).
\item[(a)] Area \(=\int_{0}^{S}(f(x)-g(x)) d x\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& =\int_{0}^{S}\left(1+\sin (2 x)-e^{x / 2}\right) d x \\
& =0.429
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(b)] Volume \(=\pi \int_{0}^{S}\left((f(x))^{2}-(g(x))^{2}\right) d x\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& =\pi \int_{0}^{S}\left((1+\sin (2 x))^{2}-\left(e^{x / 2}\right)^{2}\right) d x \\
& =4.266 \text { or } 4.267
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(c)] Volume \(=\int_{0}^{S} \frac{\pi}{2}\left(\frac{f(x)-g(x)}{2}\right)^{2} d x\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& =\int_{0}^{S} \frac{\pi}{2}\left(\frac{1+\sin (2 x)-e^{x / 2}}{2}\right)^{2} d x \\
& =0.077 \text { or } 0.078
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[1] : correct limits in an integral in (a), (b), or (c)
\item[] \(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { integrand } \\ 1: \text { answer }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[] \(3:\left\{\begin{array}{l}2: \text { integrand } \\ \langle-1\rangle \text { each error } \\ \quad \text { Note: } 0 / 2 \text { if integral not of form } \\ \quad c \int_{a}^{b}\left(R^{2}(x)-r^{2}(x)\right) d x \\ 1: \text { answer }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[] \(3:\left\{\begin{array}{l}2: \text { integrand } \\ 1: \text { answer }\end{array}\right.\)
\end{itemize}
